purpose: Stop the two production-affecting defects that survived phases 1-4: a guaranteed-wasted Chromium launch three minutes after every successful publish, and the control-panel save that silently cancels an active cooldown or maintenance pause.
design_intent: Surgical, no structural change. R1 exists to stop operational bleeding before R2 touches architecture. Every change here is a block move, a branch split, or a clamp - each independently revertable. The cheap local check must happen before the expensive network check; a pending block deadline is state, not a side effect of a setter.

model_execution_guidance.note: Small diffs, high blast radius. Each work item must land with its regression test before the next begins. Do not batch RTG-001 and RTG-003 into one commit - RTG-003 is the guard that proves RTG-001 stayed fixed.

work_items.title: Move the rate-limit gate ahead of the observer
work_items.action: Relocate both rate-limit gates - the publishBlockedUntil check (currently ~L230-260) and the STAB-001 publisherHistory 60-minute gatekeeper (currently L262-300) - to sit immediately beside the maintenance pre-flight gate, BEFORE `log = await runObserver()` at L185. The maintenance gate already has the correct shape; make the rate-limit gates match it. Note that gapInfo currently derives from the observer log; when the gate fires before the observer runs there is no log, so omit gapInfo rather than fabricating it, and confirm no caller depends on it for the rate_limited decision.
work_items.rationale: runObserver() launches Chromium at lib/observer/observerRun.ts:119. Gating after it means the platform's 1-post/hour ceiling is rediscovered by browsing the site, three minutes after we already knew we had posted.

work_items.title: Split success out of the gap_skip scheduling branch
work_items.action: At L253, `outcome.type === 'gap_skip' || outcome.type === 'success'` share the gapRecheckIntervalMinutes branch (default 3 minutes). Give 'success' its own branch that schedules the known cooldown window + 1 minute buffer. The cooldown length is known locally and needs no I/O. Keep gap_skip on gapRecheckIntervalMinutes. Use the same cooldown constant that RTG-001 reads so the two cannot drift.

work_items.title: Make an active block deadline non-shortenable
work_items.action: In scheduleNext(), after computing nextMinutes and before setTimeout, clamp the deadline: nextAt = max(now + nextMinutes, publishBlockedUntil, maintenanceBlockedUntil). Read the block timestamps from lib/state at that point. Log the clamp when it fires, with the reason that lost.
work_items.rationale: setControls / applyPreset / setIntervalMinutes (run.ts:358,365,374) each end with `void scheduleNext(false)`, which clears the pending timer and reschedules at the normal interval. routes/api/control.ts:304-312 calls setControls on every control-panel POST. Clamping at the single scheduleNext site neutralises the override trap without policing three setters.

work_items.title: Give the concurrency skip its own decision
work_items.action: Add 'already_running' to PublisherRunDecision. Return it from the guard at publisherRun.ts:483 instead of 'publisher_error'. In the scheduler tick switch, treat it as retry-in-1-minute and do not touch consecutiveFailures. Classify it in schedulerSignals.ts alongside the other non-opportunity decisions.
work_items.rationale: A manual POST /api/run-publisher overlapping a scheduler tick currently counts as a failure and triggers the 15/30/60-minute error backoff.

work_items.title: Replace the tautological cooldown tests with real gate coverage
work_items.action: Delete the two tests at publisherCooldown.test.ts:49-70 - they re-implement the cooldown arithmetic in the test body and assert against themselves, and pass with the production module deleted. Replace with: (1) a publisher run with publishBlockedUntil in the future invokes runObserver ZERO times, via an injected spy - this is the RTG-001 regression guard; (2) scheduler.setControls({}) during an active cooldown does not move nextTickEta earlier - the RTG-003 guard; (3) a 'success' outcome schedules approximately 61 minutes, not 3 - the RTG-002 guard.

acceptance_criteria: A publisher run during a known cooldown launches no browser context - asserted by spy, not by log inspection.
The run log after a verified publish shows one publish followed by one long wait, with no rate_limited entry three minutes later.
POST /api/control-panel during an active cooldown leaves nextTickEta unchanged or later, never earlier.
An overlapping manual publish run does not increment consecutiveFailures.
out_of_scope: Any change to computeEffectiveIntervalMinutes, the preset system, or the default-value duplication - that is R2.
Any change to state ownership between the scheduler closure and RuntimeStateStore - that is R3.
Maintenance detection logic - that is R4.

gate_criteria: npm run lint:structure passes with 0 errors
npm run lint passes with 0 errors
npm run test:unit passes, including the three new regression guards from RTG-005

handover_instructions.honesty_requirement: Name only files that exist and claims that were verified by a command whose output you read. The handover for phases 1-4 named lib/publisher/cooldown.ts and tests/unit/boardDiagnostics.test.ts, neither of which exists, and asserted a Chromium-launch saving the code ordering did not deliver. A handover is a map for the next session; a wrong map costs more than no map.
